clue.text: Serene clan leader in highland dress

indicators.note: the selected letter sits in, that is inside, the item of Scottish clothing

parts.note: a plaid is the tartan cloth worn over the shoulder in Highland dress

indicators.note: the leader of a group is its front member, so only the opening letter of the word clan is kept

parts.note: first letter of clan

explanation.surface: A calm Scottish chieftain stands about in full Highland costume.
explanation.walkthrough: A plaid is the long tartan wrap of traditional Scottish Highland dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid and serene are synonyms, both describing someone calm and untroubled by any agitation.

clue.text: One effecting blood transfusions for many entering General Hospital

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so the number for many is placed within the other letters

parts.note: Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A doctor at a general hospital performs blood transfusions for lots of patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General Hospital' reads as one institution, but General is Lee and Hospital is H; the hundred goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The bloodsucking worm was used by old physicians to draw off a patient's blood, so it moves blood about, humorously a transfusion.

clue.text: Escape Excise and continue with the smuggling

parts.note: to excise is to cut out
taken as written
to run is to continue, and also to smuggle, as in gun-running

explanation.surface: Customs men, the Excise, chase smugglers who carry on with their contraband trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Excise looks like the customs service from the smuggling story; here it is simply the verb meaning remove.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut and run is an idiom for fleeing hastily, from a ship cutting its anchor cable and sailing away.

clue.text: Display a lure to put an end to bold fish

indicators.note: only the end, the last letter, of the word bold is wanted

parts.note: last letter of bold
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: An angler shows off bait to stop a daring fish in its tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle bait is to hang it loosely in view as a temptation, which is exactly showing a lure.

clue.text: Order given to old soldier

parts.note: a command is an order
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A veteran trooper receives an instruction from above.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a member of an elite raiding force, a kind of specially trained soldier.

clue.text: Ideal place for gaudy bird in family to start displaying

indicators.note: the showy bird is placed in the family group, splitting its letters

parts.note: a clan is an extended family
loud colours are gaudy ones
the cuckoo is a bird

indicators.note: only the start, the opening letter, of displaying is used

parts.note: first letter of displaying

explanation.surface: A household's colourful bird begins showing off in its perfect spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird is placed inside the family word just after its first letter. The phrase comes from Aristophanes' comedy The Birds, apt for a clue about a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloud-cuckoo-land, from Aristophanes' Birds, is a fanciful utopia existing only in dreams, an unrealistic ideal realm.

clue.text: Mae truly dressed in adult fashion!

indicators.note: dressing something arranges or prepares it, so these letters are set out afresh

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Mae, perhaps Mae West, really did wear grown-up clothes!
explanation.definitionFit: Acting maturely means behaving as a grown-up would, which is acting like an adult.

clue.text: Take morsel to sustain morning's round

indicators.note: in a down entry, the lower part holds up the upper, so the bite goes beneath

parts.note: a.m. marks morning hours
a morsel taken is a bit

explanation.surface: A snack eaten to keep you going through the morning rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambit is the circuit or compass of something, its bounds, so a round in the sense of a circuit.

clue.text: Aquatic bird, low down over Thames at first, is going off course

indicators.note: in a down entry, being over something means sitting above it, so order runs top to bottom

parts.note: the diver, or loon, is a water bird
the low-down, like gen, is inside information

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the river's name is taken

parts.note: first letter of Thames

explanation.surface: A water bird flies low over the Thames and strays from its route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low down' looks like the bird's flight height; it is slang for information. GEN is British slang for the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Divergent means moving apart from a path or from each other, so departing from a set direction.

clue.text: Starting off with -preparation for display

definitions.meaning: second meaning: arranging things so they can be shown

explanation.surface: Something begins by getting goods ready to show.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both embarking on a trip and laying things out neatly, as a shop arranges its stock.

clue.text: Larks in the group — sounds like a drinking spree

definitions.note: the collective noun for larks specifically

indicators.note: these words point at how the drinking spree is pronounced rather than written

parts.note: a bevvy is British slang for a drinking session

explanation.surface: A rowdy crowd larking about sounds as though they are on a pub crawl.
explanation.walkthrough: A bevvy is British slang for a drink or a boozy night out. Larks look like fun and games but are birds, whose group name is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a company or flock, and is the traditional collective term for larks and quails.

clue.text: Fashionable English daughter's hair cut

indicators.note: read as able to be fashioned, so these letters can be shaped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A stylish English girl has had her hair cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashionable' looks like it praises the haircut; it is the anagram signal, fashion-able.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingled hair was cut in a shingle, the short tapered bob popular in the 1920s, so cropped in that style.

clue.text: About to go' home

definitions.note: a verb: to make one's way back

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a go is a turn, as in whose go is it

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of heading back to their house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to go home' reads as one phrase about leaving; split it into about, go and home.
explanation.definitionFit: To home, as pigeons do, is to travel back to base, which is what returning means.

clue.text: River erosion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the river flowing through Durham in north-east England
second meaning: gradual damage from use or friction

explanation.surface: A river's banks are being eaten away.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wear is a river in County Durham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Wear means the slow deterioration of a surface through friction, the same gradual loss as erosion.

clue.text: Just outcome of appeal held in 1 ac?

indicators.note: something held in another word is gripped inside it, so the appeal goes within the synonym

parts.note: 1 ac is short for 1 across, whose answer, meaning calm, has this synonym
it is old slang for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: A court appeal ends in a fair verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 ac' is a cross-reference: take the answer to 1 across, then a synonym of it. The question mark admits that extra step.
explanation.definitionFit: Equitable means fair and impartial, and just in this sense means fair, as in a just settlement.

clue.text: Distressed when security is relaxed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: dis-tressed, stripped of tresses, so with hair locks removed
second meaning: a door or safe left open, not fastened

explanation.surface: Someone feels upset when the guards let things slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distressed' looks like upset; read it as having lost one's tresses, and tresses are locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlocked describes a door left unfastened, and punningly a head shorn of its curls or tresses.

clue.text: Claim one called into question over right of underground worker

indicators.note: in a down entry, being over another piece means coming above it
something called into question is unsettled, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: the letters of both words
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A miner's assertion about his rights is disputed.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier digs coal from pits beneath the ground, the classic example of a subterranean labourer.

clue.text: Firm's dance on the factory floor?

parts.note: a works is a factory or manufacturing firm
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A company holds a staff dance among the machines.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a workshop is offered as a playful equivalent of the shop floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A workshop is a room or building where things are made or repaired, the production area of a factory.

clue.text: He is mainly responsible for the water supply

definitions.text: He is mainly responsible for the water supply

parts.words: He is mainly responsible for the water supply
parts.note: surface reading: a man chiefly in charge of a town's water
setter's reading: mainly means concerned with the mains, as he works the valves on water mains

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' seems to mean chiefly; it is a pun on water mains.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncock is a waterworks official who opens and closes the stopcocks controlling supply through the mains.

clue.text: Deposit in the pool may be flushed out

definitions.text: Deposit in the pool may be flushed out

parts.words: Deposit in the pool may be flushed out
parts.note: surface reading: sediment in a swimming pool that a flush of water could clear
setter's reading: a poker stake put into the pot, which may be lost to a player holding a flush

explanation.walkthrough: A flush is a poker hand of five cards in one suit; the pool is the pot of stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is the stake each poker player puts into the pot before the deal, so a payment into the kitty.

clue.text: Hounds let loose, but nothing's afoot

definitions.note: a phrase describing the state; the answer is an adjective

indicators.note: animals let loose run about freely, so these letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The pack is released, yet there's no hunt under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afoot' looks like 'happening'; here it means on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Unshod means without shoes, so with nothing on the feet, as a barefoot person or horse.

clue.text: Knocked Sunday trade

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday
truck is old word for barter or dealings, as in having no truck with

explanation.surface: Sunday trading laws are attacked or abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Sunday trading was a hot political issue in Britain in the 1990s; truck here is the old sense of exchange or dealings.
explanation.definitionFit: Struck is the past tense of strike, meaning hit, so it equals knocked.

clue.text: It's subject to ground eruption to some extent

indicators.note: only part of the next words is wanted, a stretch running across them

parts.note: letters three to seven running across the two words

explanation.surface: A place prone, in part, to volcanic outbursts from the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Under can mean governed by or liable to, as in under orders, which is being subject to something.

clue.text: Embellish book collection, with gold title

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a title is a name
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A library's books are given gilded title lettering.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in reverse of clue order: gold, then title, then the books.
explanation.definitionFit: To ornament something is to decorate it, adding beauty, which is what embellishing means.

clue.text: Requirements for son succeeding daughter born first

indicators.note: succeeding means coming after, so the son's letter follows the daughter's
the word for born is placed at the front of everything

parts.note: née, French for born, introduces a maiden name
D is the abbreviation for daughter
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Rules of inheritance where a son takes over after a firstborn daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs are things that are necessary, which is what requirements are.

clue.text: A teacher in retirement?

parts.note: taken as written
a BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teacher's degree, so stands for a teacher

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster has stopped working and drawn his pension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' suggests leaving work; here it is going to bed for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Abed means lying in bed, and retiring is going to bed for the night, so it is being in that state.

clue.text: His personnel work may result in capital gains

definitions.text: His personnel work may result in capital gains

parts.words: His personnel work may result in capital gains
parts.note: surface reading: a recruiter whose staffing work brings in profit
setter's reading: capital means of the head, so a tribal warrior collecting skulls

explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital gains' looks like finance; capital comes from the Latin for head.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a recruitment consultant who poaches executives and a warrior who collects the severed heads of enemies.

clue.text: Top rated trotting quadruped

indicators.note: trotting is lively movement, so these letters are set moving into a new order

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A first-class horse is put through its paces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrapod is any four-limbed vertebrate, from the Greek for four feet, so a four-footed animal.

clue.text: Constraint required by University when wearing gown

indicators.note: the university letter is wearing the garment, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a gown is a dress
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Academic gowns are compulsory dress at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress means coercion or compulsion by threats, a form of restraint on someone's freedom to act.
